skill.name: wiki-architect
skill.description: Analyzes code repositories and generates hierarchical documentation structures with onboarding guides. Use when the user wants to create a wiki, generate documentation, map a codebase structure, or understand a project's architecture at a high level.
skill.summary: Builds cited wiki catalogues and onboarding guides from repository structure.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and documentation wording in SKILL.md. I found no evidence of command execution, system reconnaissance intent, prompt injection, or data exfiltration.

static_findings.snippet: 5. **Cite** real files in every section prompt using `file_path:line_number`
JSON code block following the catalogue schema with `items[].children[]` structure, where each node
- System architecture Mermaid diagram, domain model ER diagram

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 26 uses Markdown backticks around the literal citation format file_path:line_number. This is not Ruby or shell backtick execution and does not define an executable command.
Line 60 uses Markdown backticks around JSON field names and structure examples. The skill contains prose output instructions, not executable shell syntax.
Line 34 asks for architecture and domain model diagrams inside generated documentation. It does not request host reconnaissance, environment probing, or sensitive system inventory.

content.value_statement: Codebase documentation often becomes generic when architecture and onboarding paths are not mapped from source files. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to build cited wiki catalogues and learning paths from the repository itself.
actual_capabilities: Scans repository structure and README context to identify project type, languages, frameworks, and architectural patterns.
Generates a hierarchical wiki catalogue with onboarding, getting started, and deep dive sections.
Requires page prompts to cite real files with file path and line number references.
Creates principal-level and zero-to-hero onboarding paths for different reader experience levels.
Applies depth and size constraints, including a simplified structure for small repositories.
limitations: Creates a documentation catalogue and prompts, not finished long-form wiki pages by default.
Depends on available repository files and README quality for accurate architecture mapping.
Does not run tests or verify runtime behavior unless the user asks through the host tool.
Requires human review for domain accuracy, roadmap guidance, and architectural judgment.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Repository Wiki
use_cases.description: Create a structured wiki outline with grounded section prompts and source citations.

use_cases.title: Accelerate Engineer Onboarding
use_cases.description: Build a learning path that moves new contributors from setup to architecture understanding.

use_cases.title: Map Legacy Architecture
use_cases.description: Turn a complex codebase into layered documentation for senior technical review.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Wiki Outline
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a complete repository wiki plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a repository wiki for this project. Scan the file tree and README, then generate the structured catalogue with cited file references.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Onboarding Path
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request focused on new contributor learning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate the onboarding section first. Include a principal-level guide and a zero-to-hero learning path based on actual source files.

prompt_templates.title: Document Architecture Layers
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this repository by presentation, business logic, data access, and infrastructure layers. Produce a wiki catalogue with architecture-focused prompts.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Deep Technical Wiki
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a detailed technical documentation structure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a depth-limited wiki catalogue for this repository. Include architecture diagrams to request, subsystem pages, component pages, file citations, and reading order.

output_examples.input: Document a TypeScript service repository for new engineers.
output_examples.output: A wiki catalogue with onboarding, setup, architecture, service layers, key components, and cited prompts for each page.

output_examples.input: Create a wiki for a small Python utility with fewer than ten files.
output_examples.output: A compact Getting Started wiki with onboarding, setup, usage, quick reference, and cited source prompts.

output_examples.input: Map a legacy application for principal engineers.
output_examples.output: An architecture-focused catalogue with strategic reading order, tradeoff prompts, diagram requests, and subsystem sections.

best_practices: Run the skill from the repository root with README and source files available.
Review every generated prompt for specific file citations before creating pages.
Validate architecture diagrams and strategic guidance with maintainers before publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not accept generic section titles that do not come from repository content.
Do not use the catalogue as a substitute for security, compliance, or API review.
Do not expand small repositories into deep documentation trees without clear need.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a structured wiki catalogue with onboarding, getting started, architecture, and deep dive sections.

faq.question: Does it write final wiki pages?
faq.answer: It primarily creates the catalogue and page prompts. Users can ask the host assistant to expand selected pages.

faq.question: Which tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How does it keep documentation grounded?
faq.answer: It instructs the assistant to reference real repository files in every generated page prompt.

faq.question: What happens with small repositories?
faq.answer: It limits small repositories to a Getting Started structure while still including onboarding content.

faq.question: Is this a security review tool?
faq.answer: No. It helps organize documentation and architecture learning, but it does not replace a security audit.
